details:
Right now, thousands of players abuse world invites and invite requests just to ask a friend a simple question like "Are you free?" or "Want to hop worlds?" It leads to accidental joins, rate limits, and a lot of unnecessary friction—especially when trying to group up between PC and Quest standalone users who don't share an easy way to message each other without taking off their headsets.

A massive chunk of the player base has been asking for a native DM system for years, but we also understand why the team has avoided text chat—it creates moderation headaches, requires storing message logs, and goes against VRChat's focus on live, face-to-face socializing.

The Solution: A Simple In-Game Smartphone Prop with Voice Calls

Instead of a text inbox, give players a lightweight, toggleable smartphone prop that handles quick friend check-ins and cleans up our current menus at the same time:

• Cross-Platform Voice Calls: Let mutual friends call each other directly across PC, Quest, and Mobile. It uses live voice audio (just like regular instance voice), meaning zero stored chat logs, no text moderation overhead, and almost zero performance cost on Quest standalone.

• Natural VR Immersion: Hearing a ringtone from your hip, pulling out the phone, and holding it to your ear to talk privately—or hitting speakerphone so friends next to you can chime in—fits VRChat's social vibe way better than staring at a wrist menu typing on a virtual keyboard.

• Dedicated Call Statuses & Missed Call Alerts: Calls only work between mutual friends, with dedicated Orange (Ask Me) and Red (Do Not Disturb) toggles specifically for the phone. If a friend tries calling while you're busy, it won't interrupt you—instead, it just leaves a simple missed-call notification showing their name and the time they tried to reach you.

• Optional FaceTime Mode (Quest-Friendly): On PC, the phone screen could show a low-res live feed of your friend's avatar so you still get that face-to-face feel. On Quest standalone, it can simply show their Impostor avatar or profile card so it never causes frame drops.

• Declutters the UI: Moving the Handheld Camera, Photo Gallery, and friend check-ins onto one grab-and-go phone prop cleans up the bloated Quick Menu and puts everything in one intuitive place.

Why This Benefits Everyone:

Players get the fast, cross-platform check-in tool they've been begging for without needing third-party overlays or external apps, and the dev team gets to keep VRChat's live, vocal social identity intact without taking on the legal and technical baggage of hosting a text messaging platform.

It solves the biggest communication gap in the game while keeping the experience immersive and lightweight on every headset.
title: VRChat shouldn't add text DMs—it should add a handheld phone with cross-platform voice calls instead
